'''Robert Culbertson West Jr.''' (March 18, 1928 – October 12, 2022) was an American chemist.

West was an E. G. Rochow Professor of Chemistry Emeritus at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]]; Director of the Organosilicon Research Center, University of Wisconsin–Madison 1999–20??; President, Silatronix, Inc. (2007–20??); Distinguished Professor, [[Yonsei University]], 2007–2011. He died in Madison, Wisconsin on October 12, 2022, at the age of 94.<ref name="obit">{{cite web|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/madison/name/robert-west-obituary?id=36945440|title=Robert West Obituary (1928–2022) – Madison, Wisconsin – Madison.com|website=[[Legacy.com]] }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Driess |first1=Matthias |last2=Apeloig |first2=Yitzhak |date=2023 |title=Robert C. West (1928–2022): A Giant in Organosilicon Chemistry, Cosmopolitan, Mountain Climber and Pilot |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/ange.202302969 |journal=Angewandte Chemie |volume=135 |issue=20 |article-number=e202302969 |doi=10.1002/ange.202302969 |bibcode=2023AngCh.135E2969D |issn=1521-3757}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Madison |title=Robert Culbertson West, Jr. Obituary Oct 12, 2022 |url=https://obits.cremationsocietyofmadison.com/robert-west-jr |access-date=2026-09-10 |website=Cremation Society of Madison |language=en}}</ref>

== Education ==
West received his Bachelor of Arts in chemistry from [[Cornell University]] in 1950, proceeding on to [[Harvard University]] where he received his Master of Arts in 1952 and Ph.D. in 1954. At Cornell, he was a member of the [[Quill and Dagger]] society.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-30 |title=In memoriam: FFRF says goodbye to remarkable scientist and member Bob West |url=https://www.freethoughttoday.com/articles/vol-39-no-10-dec-2022/in-memoriam-ffrf-says-goodbye-to-remarkable-scientist-and-member-bob-west/ |access-date=2026-09-10 |website=Freethought Today |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Notable work ==
West was a chemist best known for his groundbreaking research in [[silicon]] chemistry as well as for his work with oxocarbons and [[organolithium compound]]s. In 2004, West was listed as one of the most cited scientists during the period 1981–1999, according to a citation survey by Thomson ISI. West's most well-known discovery was the synthesis of the first ever silicon-silicon double bond in 1981, a feat which broke the so-called "double-bond rule" (which stated that main group elements below row two of the periodic table could not form double bonds). West later discovered the first example of a stable [[silylene]], a form of divalent silicon, acting as the silicon analog to the now catalytically important [[carbene]]. West also developed a new model for understanding rotations in [[polymers]]. West's numerous other discoveries include a siloxane-based [[electrolyte]] which has made possible revolutionary rechargeable implantable batteries for biomedical applications including the treatment of spinal injuries and nerve damage. His later interests included the synthesis of silicon-containing anticancer drugs, and the study of silicon and germanium compounds by [[muon]] resonance spectroscopy.

== Other interests ==
West was an instrument-rated pilot with over 2500 hours as pilot-in-command. He was a [[mountaineering|mountaineer]], with over 50 first ascents in the mountains of [[British Columbia]]. He was known for his eccentric lifestyle, liberal political views, and activism for women's reproductive rights both in the US and internationally. In 1972, along with [[Anne Nicol Gaylor]], he co-founded the Women's Medical Fund to help [[Wisconsin]] women pay for [[abortion]]s.<ref name="friendly">{{cite web | url=http://www.patheos.com/blogs/friendlyatheist/2013/10/28/four-decades-and-20000-abortions-later-anne-nicol-gaylors-organization-is-still-going-strong/ | title=Four Decades and 20,000 Abortions Later, Anne Nicol Gaylor's Organization is Still Going Strong | publisher=Patheos | work=Friendly Atheist blog | date=28 October 2013 | accessdate=14 March 2014 | author=Mehta, Hemant | authorlink=Hemant Mehta}}</ref>

His international interests led to extensive collaborative research with chemistry departments in major universities in countries including Austria, Brazil, Canada, Germany, Hungary, Israel, Japan, Korea, Lebanon, Mexico, Norway, Russia and the UK. Many of his over 600 publications were in collaboration with scientists in countries outside the USA.
